title: KV cache probe: compact experiment ledger
content:
Purpose: very small, personal sweep to see KV cache hit pattern effects on short-sequence chat workloads. Not a full experiment batch — quick, iterative notes so I can reproduce later.

SUMMARY BULLET POINTS:
- Hypothesis: enabling prefix KV caching reduces p50 for seq<=64 but may increase p95 under heavy batching due to cache eviction pressure.
- Quick wins: 1) tune cache TTL to sequence distribution, 2) limit cross-batch KV sharing for mixed-length traffic.
- Next: run 3 larger runs with TTL 15s/60s/300s and record memory + latency tails.

RUN TABLE (compact) — columns: run_id, date, model, batch_size, seq_mean, kv_enabled, cache_ttl_s, throughput_tok_s, p50_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens, notes
R1,2025-09-04,redwood-v1-8b,1,28,true,15,152,24,98,0.0045,warm cache stable; small tail spikes at minute 7
R2,2025-09-05,redwood-v1-8b,4,30,true,15,490,78,310,0.0032,throughput good; p95 worsened vs R1 under burst
R3,2025-09-06,redwood-v1-8b,4,30,false,0,410,84,220,0.0036,no cache: p95 better than R2 by ~90ms
R4,2025-09-07,redwood-v1-8b,8,12,true,60,980,19,260,0.0026,short seqs: big throughput gains, p50 excellent, p95 similar to R3
R5,2025-09-08,redwood-v1-8b,8,64,true,300,640,65,520,0.0029,longer seqs increased memory churn, p95 high

QUICK INTERPRETATION NOTES:
- Single-request runs (batch=1) with cache show best p50 but don't stress eviction.
- Batching (4-8) amplifies eviction/contention; R2 shows that enabling cache without adequate TTL/size hurts p95.
- R3 (no cache) sometimes has lower p95 under burst because system avoids cache thrash — interesting tradeoff.
- TTL 60s (R4) seems good for short interactions; TTL 300s helps reuse but memory pressure visible for seq=64 (R5).

MEASUREMENT / OBSERVABILITY CHECKLIST (notes-to-self):
- Ensure KV-hit-rate metric exported per model and per shard (tag by model, seq_bucket).
- Add lightweight flame graph capture for p95 spikes (10s windows).
- Correlate with GPU memory eviction/oom events and kernel timeouts.

REPRO STEPS (for later automation):
1) start simple client script (local) that replays 10k sessions sampled from production seq dist (seeded).
2) attach headroom monitor + kv-hit metric logging to the runtime agent.
3) vary cache_ttl [15,60,300] and batch_size [1,4,8] per run, 10k requests each.
4) gather token throughput + p50/p95 + memory RSS + eviction count.

OPEN QUESTIONS / HYPOTHESES TO TEST:
- Does selective caching (only prefix <=32 tokens) give most of the p50 benefit without eviction for longer sessions?
- Can we dynamically throttle batching when eviction rate crosses threshold to protect tail latency?

TO-DO (short):
- [ ] Add kv-hit rate to alert dashboard (priority low)
- [ ] Create a reproducible harness (script) referencing PR 482
- [ ] Share quick findings with @infra and @sre next Tuesday

SCRATCH / RAW COMMANDS (local):
# run quick replay (dev box)
python infra/tools/replay.py --model redwood-v1-8b --batch 4 --seed 42 --count 10000 --kv-ttl 15 --out run_r2.json
# quick extract metrics
jq -r '.metrics | {throughput: .tokens_per_sec, p50: .latency.p50_ms, p95: .latency.p95_ms}' run_r2.json

END NOTES: this file is my ephemeral ledger for tuning cache defaults. Move to shared drive /confluence if we decide on defaults or produce a short proposal.
